vignette: 34-year-old woman with six months of fatigue and diffuse aches. She has Hashimoto's thyroiditis; joints, skin and urine are normal on exam. The ANA was sent as a 'screen'.
teach: An exact 1:80 slightly lowers the odds of SLE, and thyroid disease raises background ANA. Fatigue and aches are not an indication. No ENA, no repeat ANA.

vignette: 41-year-old woman with vague joint aching but no swelling or stiffness. Exam is normal. The lab confirmed isolated anti-DFS70 antibodies.
teach: A confirmed monospecific DFS70 pattern with no objective features is reassuring in adults, even at 1:320. It would not be reassuring in a child.

vignette: 52-year-old woman with three years of biphasic Raynaud's and puffy fingers. No dyspnea, ulcers or rash. The lab reports a centromere pattern.
teach: Raynaud plus a centromere pattern is a very-early-SSc picture. Skip the broad ENA; check ALP/AMA (PBC), echo and PFTs with DLCO, and refer.

vignette: 28-year-old woman with symmetric swelling of three joints and morning stiffness over 45 minutes. WBC is 3.1 with no other cause. ANA is homogeneous.
teach: Two organ systems put pre-test probability above 50% before the ANA is even read. A modest titer does not cap that risk. Send the referral with dsDNA, C3/C4 and urine already done.

vignette: 45-year-old man with fatigue only. His ANA was added to a routine panel and is very high. Exam and basic labs are normal.
teach: Even a very high titer leaves disease improbable with no features, so no referral. But the fine speckled pattern warrants a short targeted step: re-take the history, then SSA/SSB, not an 11-antibody panel.

vignette: 30-year-old woman with ankle swelling and foamy urine for two weeks. Urine protein:creatinine ratio is 1.2 with red cells in the sediment. ANA is 1:80.
teach: A red flag overrides a low titer. A new active urinary sediment needs same-day assessment and urgent rheumatology input.

vignette: 40-year-old woman with generalized aching and no objective findings. The lab reports a 'dense fine speckled-like' pattern at 1:320 but has not run an anti-DFS70 assay.
teach: About half of labs mis-call DFS. Confirm monospecific anti-DFS70 before reassuring anyone; that is the one targeted order.

vignette: Nine-year-old with intermittent knee pain after sport. Joints are normal, no rash, no eye symptoms. ANA 1:320, fine speckled.
teach: In a well child with a titer below 1:640 the ANA may be disregarded. ANA adds nothing for undiagnosed musculoskeletal pain in children.

vignette: 46-year-old woman with two years of dry eyes and mouth. Schirmer's test is 3 mm in five minutes; no joint, skin or urine findings. ANA is fine speckled.
teach: Objective sicca plus a fine speckled pattern is a Sjogren pathway: order anti-SSA/Ro and SSB/La, plus baseline CBC and urinalysis. You don't need a full ENA.
